Q: Mr. Grubbs, I'm showing you what has been marked as Exhibit 57 to the depositions. (Whereupon, Exhibit 57 was identified.) Do you see the mortgage on the screen?
A: Yes.

Q: And do you see that Ms. Deborah Hogan's name is stamped at the top as instrument prepared by and returned to?

Q: Do you have any knowledge regarding Ms. Hogan's role in preparing this document, apart from the fact that her name appears at the top left corner?

Q: Do you have any information, other than the fact that her name is printed at the top, regarding what her role was in preparing the document?
A: No.

Q: Did you ever specifically ask Ms. Hogan to prepare any documents?
A: All documents were produced in conversations between Tom Hogan, Vic, and myself.

Q: Did you ever ask Ms. Hogan directly to prepare a legal instrument for you?
A: No, not directly.

Q: Did Ms. Hogan ever negotiate any deals for you?
A: No.

Q: Did Ms. Hogan ever negotiate any deals for Grubbs Construction Company?
A: No.

Q: Okay. This is Exhibit Tab 35 in Mr. Persante's binder. Do you recall an extensive examination you had with Mr. Persante about this assignment of contract?
A: Scroll down. All right. Scroll down. Okay. What was your question?

Q: Do you recall signing this with witnesses present? I see that there are no signatures there.
A: No.

Q: Do you have any personal knowledge about Ms. Hogan's role in preparing this document?
A: Other than it indicates on the face of this document that she did.

Q: Beyond the fact that her name appears at the top left corner, do you have any information regarding the role she played in drafting the document?
A: No. I wasn't present when it was drafted.

Q: Okay. I'm sharing Exhibit 65 to the depositions. I'll give you a second to review the exhibit. I can scroll through if you need to, but do you recognize this?
A: Yes. (Whereupon, Tab 65 was identified.)

Q: Do you know who drafted this document?
A: The Hogan Law Firm.

Q: Do you know which professional at the Hogan Law Firm drafted this document?
A: I wasn't present when it was being drafted.

Q: So the answer is no, you don't know who at Hogan Law Firm drafted this document?
A: No.

Q: Okay. Did you ask that Exhibit 65 be drafted?
A: What's that?

Q: Did you ask, sir, that Exhibit 65 -- MR. FOREMAN: Mike, your outline -- your questions are on the screen? MR. ARENDALL: Oh, sorry. BY MR. ARENDALL: Did you ask, Mr. Grubbs, that this Consulting Agreement be drafted?
A: No.

Q: Do you know who asked that it be drafted?
A: No.

Q: I'm showing you what's been marked as Tab 77 to Mr. Persante's group of exhibits. Do you remember talking with him about this Promissory Note for $500,267?
A: Yes.

Q: And just to recall, this is the Promissory Note that you gave to Grubbs Construction Company as part of your purchase of shares of that company, correct?
A: Yes.

Q: Mr. Grubbs, do you still own the 2,688 shares of stock that you purchased in Grubbs Construction Company?
A: As far as I know.

Q: Did you expect to lose those shares when you failed to pay this Promissory Note?
A: I didn't know what to expect.

Q: As we sit here today though, even though you testified that you did not pay this Promissory Note you still own those shares, correct?
A: As far as I know, I do.

Other than Ms. Hogan's name appearing at the top left corner, do you have any information regarding Ms. Hogan's role in preparing this Assignment of Interest?
A: Other than what it states on the document, that she prepared it.

Q: Other than that, no other information regarding her role?
A: No.

A: Yes.

Q: The Minutes reflect that Ms. Deborah Hogan was present. Do you recall her being at this meeting November 25th, 2015?
A: She could have been.

Q: But as we sit here today you do not recall her being there?
A: She could have been.

Q: Could she have been based on the Minutes or based on your own personal recollection of you?
A: My personal recollection.

Q: Do you remember Ms. Stanfield as being there at the meeting?
A: It's very possible, yes.

Q: I want to zero in on the paragraph that begins, Vic Taglia moved that the corporation take the recommended steps. Do you see that paragraph, Mr. Grubbs?
A: Yes.

Q: The paragraph continues, number one, to confirm that the personal expenses and personal activities shall not be paid from the corporation's funds. My question is, did Ms. Hogan have any input on this motion number one?
A: No.

Q: And the motion continues as number two, to reaffirm the 2008 corporate restructuring with respect to any commonly-owned entities. And it continues. Did Ms. Hogan have any role in motion number two?
A: Not that I know of.

Q: Did Ms. Hogan say anything during this meeting?
A: Not that I can particularly remember.

Q: Did you take any notes, Mr. Grubbs, of this meeting?
A: No.

Q: Okay. And the paragraph that says in the center of the page, Gary Grubbs disclosed that the IRS currently seeks payment from him, Gary, of $750,000. Do you see that paragraph?
A: Yes.

Q: At the end of that paragraph the sentence reads, he confirmed that he does not have any money with which to pay these demands. Do you see that?
A: Yes.

Q: Was that a true statement as of November 25th, 2015?
A: I was in the process of remedying this problem at that time.

Q: Did an attorney with Hogan Law Firm ever discuss how creditors can get a court order to take someone's stock in a corporation, but not take their membership in a limited liability company?
A: That wasn't explained to me like that.

Q: Okay. You and Mr. Persante spoke about the issue briefly yesterday. Do you understand that distinction sitting here today?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. If the Minutes reflect that that discussion occurred, do you have any reason to believe that it did not occur?
A: Yes, I have a reason to believe that it didn't occur, because there's a lot of -- you know, there's things that we talked about that just don't show up. I don't remember exactly what it was, but there's a lot of things we talked about over the years.

Q: Well, I appreciate your testimony that there were things that you talked about that didn't show up in the Minutes. This would be the opposite of that, which would be there were Minutes of a discussion that you can't remember ever having. Is that a true statement?
A: Repeat the question.

Q: I appreciate that your testimony has been that there were pieces of information that were discussed at meetings that never made it into the Minutes, correct?
A: Correct.

Q: But with respect to corporate law and Mr. Hogan's counsel that a creditor can get a court order to take shares of a corporation but do not get the actual membership interest in a limited liability company, the Minutes reflect that as being a discussion point. Do you recall that discussion happening?
A: No.

A: What are you asking?

Q: I'm asking if you objected for disagreed with any actions taken by Sun West Acquisition Corporation at this meeting on November 25th, 2015. MR. DEEB: Object to form. THE WITNESS: How could I object to the contents when I didn't know the contents of the Minutes of the meetings prior. BY MR. ARENDALL: Do you Object, Mr. -- do you disagree, Mr. Grubbs, that you were sitting in a chair in the conference room during this meeting?

A: If I had any objections at the time. It was a meeting. We talked about certain things.

Q: And these Minutes reflect the occurrence of that meeting, correct?
A: They reflect the occurrence. Yeah, it's obvious that the meeting occurred. Yes, the meeting occurred.

Q: And that 2015 meeting on November 25th, 2015 was happening in the midst of the Internal Revenue Service action against Sun West Acquisition Corporation, correct?
A: You cut out there, Michael. Say it again.

Q: Certainly. The November 25th, 2015 meeting that we just looked at the Minutes of what happening in the midst of an Internal Revenue Service action to take certain funds of Sun West Acquisition Corporation, correct?
A: They had already done that.

Q: Part of the discussion point for that meeting was to talk about how the company would respond to the IRS action. Isn't that true?
A: Yes.

Q: One of the discussion points was to have mortgages recorded by Dial One on Sun West Acquisition Corporation property. Isn't that true?
A: It was bought up and not agreed upon.

Q: Would you consider it a strategic business decision to have mortgages recorded on property if the mortgages have already been given?
A: The property was debt free. The mortgage -- what mortgages were set inside, set in the files or in-house were just created. It was a strategy that was determined to be used and advised by Tom and Vic.

Q: Well, do you understand why a mortgage would be recorded on a piece of property when a creditor is threatening adverse action?
A: I've tried to live a debt-free life, and it bothered me to have mortgages on properties that we paid for ourselves.

Q: So to be clear, the notes were given from Sun West Acquisition Corporation to Dial One, correct?
A: Yes.

Q: But it was important from a strategic perspective, as this was part of the November 25th, 2015 meeting discussion, to have mortgages recorded in order to protect assets of Sun West Acquisition Corporation, correct? MR. DEEB: Object to form. THE WITNESS: That was -- that was something that they were talking about. I did not support that. Whether it's a good practice or not, I don't agree with it. BY MR. Would that have been a preferred outcome for you?
A: Well, it set there unrecorded for many years, so I don't know why all of the sudden everybody's getting in a panic mode. I was able to facilitate the issues I had with the IRS and settle the issues with Sun West Acquisitions, got their money collected.

Q: The paragraph continues, Grubbs has a long-standing relationship of trust and confidence with the Hogans. Is this a true statement?
A: Yes.

Q: Do you see at the beginning of paragraph 13 of your Complaint it reads, during this time Grubbs was represented by Tom Hogan, Deborah Hogan, and the Hogan Law Firm?
A: Yes.

Q: What do you mean when you say during this time?

Q: And when did the purchase of Sun West happen?
A: '99. January 20th of '99.

My question is, what did you mean by during this time? MR. DEEB: Object to form. THE WITNESS: During the time of the purchase. BY MR. ARENDALL: So this paragraph -- the words of this paragraph, during this time, are meant by you to mean during the purchase of Sun West in January of 1999?
A: Yes, on this particular purchase.

Q: Well, what does this particular purchase mean?
A: Sun West property.

Q: Okay.
A: That's what that says, refers back to.

Q: Did -- when you say Grubbs had a long-standing relationship of trust and confidence with the Hogans, do you mean both Tom Hogan and Deborah Hogan?
